AFTERMATH — Every Failure Should Leave a Safeguard. Recorded from the live production deployment at aftermath-7tij.vercel.app
A claim is not evidence. When an AI agent says the work succeeded, AFTERMATH asks for the proof — and when a failure is verified, it leaves a safeguard so the same failure cannot recur unnoticed.
The investigation workspace is now public. A visitor can open the product's core act without a credential; the operator console remains separate and gated.
Paste the incident: a charge request returned 503, was retried, and an agent then claimed success. AFTERMATH parses the material as data — it is never executed.
Safeguard Records: every investigation, newest first. Each record is a connected chain — incident, evidence, hypothesis, safeguard, verification, and memory.
Each record states honestly how far its safeguard is verified: simulated, live, or recall-verified. Nothing is presented as more than it is.
The Memory Ledger reads live Walrus Memory Mainnet state from the relayer: authentication, the namespace, and the persisted memories.
Completed writes and recall-verified writes are counted from durable records. Simulated writes are excluded, and each write is confirmed by a recall query.
The learning loop end to end: investigate, learn, persist to Walrus Memory, recall during a later investigation, change a decision, and verify the change.
Learning impact — every figure counted from durable records: memories recalled, memories applied, investigations influenced, and requirements strengthened.

Behaviour change is a real counterfactual: the same decision engine run twice, once with the recalled safeguard held out and once enforced. The difference is the memory's own contribution — here it added required verification checks.
Provenance closes the loop: the safeguard links back to the incident that produced it, its Walrus blob reference, and every later investigation it reached. Every failure should leave a safeguard.
